title: Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv
statement: Prove that among any $2n - 1$ integers one can choose $n$ whose sum is divisible by $n$.
hints: Show the statement is multiplicative: if it holds for $a$ and for $b$, it holds for $ab$.
For a prime $p$, apply the Chevalley–Warning theorem over $\mathbb{F}_p$ to $\sum a_i x_i^{p-1}$ and $\sum x_i^{p-1}$ in $2p-1$ variables.
solution: Multiplicativity. Given $2ab-1$ integers, repeatedly remove $a$ of them with sum divisible by $a$; this is possible while at least $2a-1$ remain, which gives $2b-1$ groups. Divide each group sum by $a$ and apply the case $b$ to these $2b-1$ quotients: $b$ groups, $ab$ numbers, sum divisible by $ab$. Primes. Over $\mathbb{F}_p$ take $f_1 = \sum a_i x_i^{p-1}$ and $f_2 = \sum x_i^{p-1}$ in $2p-1$ variables. The degrees add to $2p-2 < 2p-1$, so by Chevalley–Warning the number of common zeros is divisible by $p$. The zero vector is one, so another exists. Its support has size divisible by $p$ (from $f_2$) and between $1$ and $2p-1$, so it is exactly $p$, and $f_1$ says those $a_i$ sum to $0 \bmod p$.

rubric.criterion: the multiplicative reduction, stated and proved
the prime case, by Chevalley–Warning or Cauchy–Davenport
